analyst_view.overall: Bottom-three Sassuolo (18th, 8 points, six league defeats in a row and no win since mid-September) host Napoli (8th, 18 points). Roberto D'Aversa lost his first game 2-0 to Genoa and, after trying a back three, is now expected to go back to a 4-3-3 with Berardi and Laurienté wide and Bowie or Esposito in the middle; Adzic, Leysen (counted), Kone and Boloca are out, Volpato and Bakola doubtful. Napoli come from a 2-2 at Manchester City on Tuesday, their starters only did recovery work afterwards, and Allegri has seven out: Meret, Lobotka, Vergara, Alisson Santos, Badiashile and Di Lorenzo (all in the numbers) plus Buongiorno (not in the numbers), with Rafa Marin back from his ban. Referee Marco Guida (3.6 cards a game) is now in the numbers. Since yesterday I drop my goals trim because Sassuolo are no longer switching to a more defensive back three, and keep only a small trim on shots for a tired Napoli.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals (0.8 Sassuolo, 1.7 Napoli); they already add Sassuolo's 21 goals conceded in six games and take off the injured players on both sides. Yesterday I trimmed for D'Aversa's back three, but he is now expected back in a 4-3-3, and Buongiorno's absence from Napoli's defence (not counted) offsets Napoli's tiredness after Manchester City, so I stay at about 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners and already add some for Sassuolo because Napoli have conceded 41 corners in their last six games. Sassuolo's 4-3-3 with Berardi and Laurienté wide and Napoli's wing-backs Politano and Spinazzola both use the flanks, and nothing points clearly either way, so I stay at about 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.1 cards; they already take a little off for referee Marco Guida (3.6 a game, just under the league average) and for Sassuolo's low card count lately. A side in a relegation fight under a new coach can play with more edge, but Napoli tend to manage games under Allegri and I found nothing pointing to a heated match, so I stay at about 3.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.3 shots and already add +8% for Napoli's recent shooting against a Sassuolo side that conceded 105 shots in six games. Napoli play four days after a draining night at the Etihad with a squad described as decimated, and Allegri has to manage his players' energy, so I trim mildly to about 26.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target and already add +13% for Napoli's accuracy in their last six games, while Sassuolo have managed only 17 on target in that run. For the same reason as shots, a tired Napoli after the Champions League, I trim slightly to about 9.1.
